incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT detected: Streaming p99 latency spike for hosted int8 profile (us-west-2). Metric breach: p99 latency 2.8s (SLO 1.2s) across 3 clusters. Auto-alert created. thread id=2112345678

marie.ops: seeing the same in console — p95 up ~600ms, p99 jump to 2.8s. Mostly streaming RPCs, not batch. :thinking_face:

taylor_oncall: I'm on it. Paging raj.sre and sam.eng. Any customer-facing errors?

customer-success: A couple customers on dedicated plans reported timeouts for long-stream sessions. Reporting degraded convo quality and reconnects. No data exfiltration.

raj.sre: grabbing logs now, starting a correlation search for `model_profile=int8` and `stream=true`. Initial note: spike aligns with 04:12 UTC — that lines up with yesterday's int8 calibration roll to stable.

sam.eng: confirmed — the rollout finished 04:05 UTC. Canary looked fine, but we ramped to 70% at 04:08 and 100% by 04:11.

alex_ml: calibration jobs completed successfully but we saw higher variance in KV cache hit rates for long-context requests under int8. Might be causing extra dequant/decompress churn.

raj.sre: stack traces show a lot of `KVCache::page_fault` events and `dequant_step` stalls. Typical symptom: increased per-token overhead for tails.

marie.ops: any easy rollback path? We need something quick to stop customer impact.

sam.eng: We can hit the routing policy to route streaming requests to the fp8-compatible model variant as fallback. Planning: 1) add temporary routing rule 2) scale fp8 pool by +20% 3) throttle int8 allocations.

taylor_oncall: do it. If that fails, roll back the int8 profile for the affected model to previous quantized artifact. I can push the canary rollback.

raj.sre: I'm running the routing change now: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/v1/routing -d '{"match":{"profile":"int8","stream":true},"route_to":"fp8_variant","priority":100}'` — applying...

incident-bot: Change submitted by raj.sre at 04:25 UTC. Policy ID: rp-4581.

sam.eng: scaling fp8 pool: `./infra/scale_pool --pool fp8-usw2 --delta 12` — command completed, 12 nodes added, warm-up in progress.

marie.ops: seeing immediate drop in p99 on the int8 pool from 2.8s -> 1.4s, but overall p99 for streaming cluster is 1.6s and trending down.

customer-success: Customers reporting reduced reconnects, thanks. Still seeing a few degraded sessions from older clients.

alex_ml: digging deeper: calibration change introduced a different quantization layout for KV shards which increases dequant cost when cache miss rates climb. For short sessions fine, but tails of streaming (long contexts) hit the worst-case path.

raj.sre: recommended follow-ups: 1) revert quant artifact for model X to `v1.2-int8` -> `v1.1-int8` if routing override doesn't fully fix 2) add KVCache metrics + alerts for dequant stalls 3) throttle long-context requests or provide backpressure to clients.

taylor_oncall: Agree. I'll prepare a rollback patch but prefer to keep routing for now to avoid churn. Can someone run a focused canary with long-context synthetic load against both variants?

sam.eng: launching canary harness: `python tools/benchmark_stream.py --model model-x --profiles int8,fp8 --mode long-context --rps 50 --duration 15m --tag 'calib-triage'` — will report within 20m.

marie.ops: FYI we also saw an uptick in model preemption logs — nodes getting evicted while serving long streams. Could be autoscaler interaction due to higher latencies.

raj.sre: I temporarily bumped eviction thresholds and disabled aggressive downscale for the fp8 pool to prevent warm-up churn. Patch: `autoscaler.disable_scale_down(pool=fp8-usw2, ttl=600)` applied.

incident-bot: Severity escalated to SEV3 at 04:40 UTC due to customer impact on Dedicated customers. Paging oncall lead.

customer-success: opening tickets for the impacted customers, adding mitigation notes and ETA.

alex_ml: can we capture a small trace for one of the affected traces? `trace_id=abc123` shows frequent `DequantKernel::exec` taking 30-50ms each on tail tokens vs 2-4ms historically. That's a 10-20x regression for tail operations.

marie.ops: interesting — that would perfectly explain p99 tails. Any idea why calibration would cause such regression?

alex_ml: likely changes in per-layer quant scales leading to more expensive dequant math paths (fallback code paths on certain ranges). We'll diff the calibration artifacts.

sam.eng: can we hotpatch runtime to use the faster dequant kernel variant for int8? Risky in prod but may be faster than full rollback.

raj.sre: hotpatch proposal evaluated: needs a quick build and a controlled rollout to canaries. Time estimate 30–45m; with risk of introducing CPU/GPU regression. Prefer routing to fp8 until canary proves safe.

taylor_oncall: agreed. Keep routing in place, continue canary. Start rollback plan in background. Notify sales/CS for any enterprise customers asking for credits.

incident-bot: Routing rule rp-4581 currently matches ~42% of streaming requests and is expected to reach 60% as traffic rebalances. Next automated check in 5m.

sam.eng: canary results (10m in): fp8 p99=1.1s, int8 p99=2.6s under long-context synthetic load. Breakdown shows int8 dequant stall spikes at token offsets >1024.

marie.ops: That's a clear repro. Given footprint and customer impact, I'm going to trigger rollback of the int8 quant artifact for model-x to the prior stable artifact. Initiating rollback: `models.rollback --model model-x --artifact v1.2-int8 --target v1.1-int8 --reason 'tail latency regression'`

raj.sre: rollback job created: job-id rj-9921. Monitoring job.

incident-bot: Rollback job rj-9921 started at 05:12 UTC. Will stream events here.

sam.eng: job patch applied to control plane; starting gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with 3m observation windows.

marie.ops: p99 trending down now cluster-wide: 1.3s -> 1.05s as rollback ramps to 50%.

customer-success: Customers confirm recovery, some still reporting intermittent issues but much improved.

taylor_oncall: I'll keep the routing rule active until rollback completes and we confirm stability for 24h. Also assign follow-ups: `SRE-287` add dequant stalls alert, `ML-512` root cause analysis of calibration diff, `ENG-724` add safer rollout gating for quant calibration.

alex_ml: will produce a diff of calibration histograms and a patch to force stable scale quantization for tails.

raj.sre: leaving a note for postmortem: timeline, why canary missed tail case, improve canary workloads to include long-context streaming and KV cache miss patterns.

marie.ops: final status: rollback rj-9921 completed at 05:38 UTC, cluster p99=1.02s, p95=320ms. Routing rule will be removed by oncall after 24h stable.

taylor_oncall: great work team. We'll keep monitoring dashboards and schedule postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PST. I'll write a short incident summary for customers. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident resolved at 05:38 UTC (SEV3 -> Resolved). Tags: quantization, rollback, routing-mitigation, tail-latency.
